NKJV.1: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out to battle against the Philistines, and encamped beside Ebenezer; and the Philistines encamped in Aphek.
NKJV.2: Then the Philistines put themselves in battle array against Israel. And when they joined battle, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men of the army in the field.
NKJV.3: And when the people had come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh to us, that when it comes among us it may save us from the hand of our enemies.”
NKJV.4: So the people sent to Shiloh, that they might bring from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who dwells between the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
NKJV.5: And when the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, all Israel shouted so loudly that the earth shook.
NKJV.6: Now when the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, “What does the sound of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” Then they understood that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.
NKJV.7: So the Philistines were afraid, for they said, “God has come into the camp!” And they said, “Woe to us! For such a thing has never happened before.
NKJV.8: Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness.
NKJV.9: Be strong and conduct yourselves like men, you Philistines, that you do not become servants of the Hebrews, as they have been to you. Conduct yourselves like men, and fight!”
NKJV.10: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and every man fled to his tent. There was a very great slaughter, and there fell of Israel thirty thousand foot soldiers.
NKJV.11: Also the ark of God was captured; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
NKJV.12: Then a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line the same day, and came to Shiloh with his clothes torn and dirt on his head.
NKJV.13: Now when he came, there was Eli, sitting on a seat by the wayside watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came into the city and told it, all the city cried out.
NKJV.14: When Eli heard the noise of the outcry, he said, “What does the sound of this tumult mean?” And the man came quickly and told Eli.
NKJV.15: Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were so dim that he could not see.
NKJV.16: Then the man said to Eli, “I am he who came from the battle. And I fled today from the battle line.” And he said, “What happened, my son?”
NKJV.17: So the messenger answered and said, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. Also your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead; and the ark of God has been captured.”
NKJV.18: Then it happened, when he made mention of the ark of God, that Eli fell off the seat backward by the side of the gate; and his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.
NKJV.19: Now his daughter-in-law, Phinehas’s wife, was with child, due to be delivered; and when she heard the news that the ark of God was captured, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth, for her labor pains came upon her.
NKJV.20: And about the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, “Do not fear, for you have borne a son.” But she did not answer, nor did she regard it.
NKJV.21: Then she named the child Ichabod, saying, “The glory has departed from Israel!” because the ark of God had been captured and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
NKJV.22: And she said, “The glory has departed from Israel, for the ark of God has been captured.”

ESV.1: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out to battle against the Philistines. They encamped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines encamped at Aphek.
ESV.2: The Philistines drew up in line against Israel, and when the battle spread, Israel was defeated before the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men on the field of battle.
ESV.3: And when the people came to the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD here from Shiloh, that it  may come among us and save us from the power of our enemies.”
ESV.4: So the people sent to Shiloh and brought from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned on the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
ESV.5: As soon as the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, all Israel gave a mighty shout, so that the earth resounded.
ESV.6: And when the Philistines heard the noise of the shouting, they said, “What does this great shouting in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” And when they learned that the ark of the LORD had come to the camp,
ESV.7: the Philistines were afraid, for they said, “A god has come into the camp.” And they said, “Woe to us! For nothing like this has happened before.
ESV.8: Woe to us! Who can deliver us from the power of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with every sort of plague in the wilderness.
ESV.9: Take courage, and be men, O Philistines, lest you become slaves to the Hebrews as they have been to you; be men and fight.”
ESV.10: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and they fled, every man to his home. And there was a very great slaughter, for thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.
ESV.11: And the ark of God was captured, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
ESV.12: A man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh the same day, with his clothes torn and with dirt on his head.
ESV.13: When he arrived, Eli was sitting on his seat by the road watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came into the city and told the news, all the city cried out.
ESV.14: When Eli heard the sound of the outcry, he said, “What is this uproar?” Then the man hurried and came and told Eli.
ESV.15: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old and his eyes were set so that he could not see.
ESV.16: And the man said to Eli, “I am he who has come from the battle; I fled from the battle today.” And he said, “How did it go, my son?”
ESV.17: He who brought the news answered and said, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has also been a great defeat among the people. Your two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been captured.”
ESV.18: As soon as he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell over backward from his seat by the side of the gate, and his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.
ESV.19: Now his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant, about to give birth. And when she heard the news that the ark of God was captured, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed and gave birth, for her pains came upon her.
ESV.20: And about the time of her death the women attending her said to her, “Do not be afraid, for you have borne a son.” But she did not answer or pay attention.
ESV.21: And she named the child Ichabod, saying, “The glory has departed  from Israel!” because the ark of God had been captured and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
ESV.22: And she said, “The glory has departed from Israel, for the ark of God has been captured.”

NASB.1: Thus the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle and camped beside Ebenezer while the Philistines camped in Aphek.
NASB.2: The Philistines drew up in battle array to meet Israel. When the battle spread, Israel was defeated before the Philistines who killed about four thousand men on the battlefield.
NASB.3: When the people came into the camp, the elders of Israel said, 'Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us take to ourselves from Shiloh the ark of the covenant of the LORD, that it may come among us and deliver us from the power of our enemies.'
NASB.4: So the people sent to Shiloh, and from there they carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts who sits [above] the cherubim; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, [were] there with the ark of the covenant of God.
NASB.5: As the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth resounded.
NASB.6: When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, 'What [does] the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews [mean]?' Then they understood that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.
NASB.7: The Philistines were afraid, for they said, 'God has come into the camp.' And they said, 'Woe to us! For nothing like this has happened before.
NASB.8: 'Woe to us! Who shall deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who smote the Egyptians with all [kinds of] plagues in the wilderness.
NASB.9: 'Take courage and be men, O Philistines, or you will become slaves to the Hebrews, as they have been slaves to you; therefore, be men and fight.'
NASB.10: So the Philistines fought and Israel was defeated, and every man fled to his tent; and the slaughter was very great, for there fell of Israel thirty thousand foot soldiers.
NASB.11: And the ark of God was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
NASB.12: Now a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh the same day with his clothes torn and dust on his head.
NASB.13: When he came, behold, Eli was sitting on [his] seat by the road eagerly watching, because his heart was trembling for the ark of God. So the man came to tell [it] in the city, and all the city cried out.
NASB.14: When Eli heard the noise of the outcry, he said, 'What [does] the noise of this commotion [mean]?' Then the man came hurriedly and told Eli.
NASB.15: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were set so that he could not see.
NASB.16: The man said to Eli, 'I am the one who came from the battle line. Indeed, I escaped from the battle line today.' And he said, 'How did things go, my son?'
NASB.17: Then the one who brought the news replied, 'Israel has fled before the Philistines and there has also been a great slaughter among the people, and your two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been taken.'
NASB.18: When he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell off the seat backward beside the gate, and his neck was broken and he died, for he was old and heavy. Thus he judged Israel forty years.
NASB.19: Now his daughter-in-law, Phinehas's wife, was pregnant and about to give birth; and when she heard the news that the ark of God was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, she kneeled down and gave birth, for her pains came upon her.
NASB.20: And about the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, 'Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son.' But she did not answer or pay attention.
NASB.21: And she called the boy Ichabod, saying, 'The glory has departed from Israel,' because the ark of God was taken and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
NASB.22: She said, 'The glory has departed from Israel, for the ark of God was taken.'

NLT.1: And Samuel’s words went out to all the people of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Ark At that time Israel was at war with the Philistines. The Israelite army was camped near Ebenezer, and the Philistines were at Aphek.
NLT.2: The Philistines attacked and defeated the army of Israel, killing 4,000 men.
NLT.3: After the battle was over, the troops retreated to their camp, and the elders of Israel asked, “Why did the LORD allow us to be defeated by the Philistines?” Then they said, “Let’s bring the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD from Shiloh. If we carry it into battle with us, it will save us from our enemies.”
NLT.4: So they sent men to Shiloh to bring the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD of Heaven’s Armies, who is enthroned between the cherubim. Hophni and Phinehas, the sons of Eli, were also there with the Ark of the Covenant of God.
NLT.5: When all the Israelites saw the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD coming into the camp, their shout of joy was so loud it made the ground shake!
NLT.6: “What’s going on?” the Philistines asked. “What’s all the shouting about in the Hebrew camp?” When they were told it was because the Ark of the LORD had arrived,
NLT.7: they panicked. “The gods have come into their camp!” they cried. “This is a disaster! We have never had to face anything like this before!
NLT.8: Help! Who can save us from these mighty gods of Israel? They are the same gods who destroyed the Egyptians with plagues when Israel was in the wilderness.
NLT.9: Fight as never before, Philistines! If you don’t, we will become the Hebrews’ slaves just as they have been ours! Stand up like men and fight!”
NLT.10: So the Philistines fought desperately, and Israel was defeated again. The slaughter was great; 30,000 Israelite soldiers died that day. The survivors turned and fled to their tents.
NLT.11: The Ark of God was captured, and Hophni and Phinehas, the two sons of Eli, were killed.
NLT.12: A man from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefield and arrived at Shiloh later that same day. He had torn his clothes and put dust on his head to show his grief.
NLT.13: Eli was waiting beside the road to hear the news of the battle, for his heart trembled for the safety of the Ark of God. When the messenger arrived and told what had happened, an outcry resounded throughout the town.
NLT.14: “What is all the noise about?” Eli asked. The messenger rushed over to Eli,
NLT.15: who was ninety-eight years old and blind.
NLT.16: He said to Eli, “I have just come from the battlefield — I was there this very day.” “What happened, my son?” Eli demanded.
NLT.17: “Israel has been defeated by the Philistines,” the messenger replied. “The people have been slaughtered, and your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were also killed. And the Ark of God has been captured.”
NLT.18: When the messenger mentioned what had happened to the Ark of God, Eli fell backward from his seat beside the gate. He broke his neck and died, for he was old and overweight. He had been Israel’s judge for forty years.
NLT.19: Eli’s daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and near her time of delivery. When she heard that the Ark of God had been captured and that her father-in-law and husband were dead, she went into labor and gave birth.
NLT.20: She died in childbirth, but before she passed away the midwives tried to encourage her. “Don’t be afraid,” they said. “You have a baby boy!” But she did not answer or pay attention to them.
NLT.21: She named the child Ichabod (which means “Where is the glory?”), for she said, “Israel’s glory is gone.” She named him this because the Ark of God had been captured and because her father-in-law and husband were dead.
NLT.22: Then she said, “The glory has departed from Israel, for the Ark of God has been captured.”

AMP.6: When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, "What does the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews mean?" Then they understood that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.
AMP.7: The Philistines were afraid, for they said, "God has come into the camp." And they said, "Woe [disaster is coming] to us! For nothing like this has happened before.
AMP.8: Woe to us! Who will rescue us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
AMP.9: Take courage, and be men, O Philistines, so that you do not become servants to the Hebrews, as they have been servants to you; act like men and fight!"
AMP.10: So the Philistines fought; Israel was defeated and every man fled to his tent. It was a very great defeat, for thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.
AMP.11: Also the ark of God was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were killed.
AMP.12: Now a man [from the tribe] of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh that same day with his clothes torn and dust on his head [as signs of mourning over the disaster].
AMP.13: When he arrived, Eli was sitting on his seat by the road, keeping watch, because his heart was anxious about the ark of God. When the man arrived to report [the news] in the city, everyone in the city cried out [to God, for help].
AMP.14: When Eli heard the noise of the outcry, he asked, "What is the noise of this uproar?" And the man came hurriedly and told Eli.
AMP.15: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old; his eyes were dim so that he could not see.
AMP.16: The man said to Eli, "I have come from the battle line. Indeed, I escaped from the battle line today." Eli said, "How did things go, my son?"
AMP.17: The messenger replied, "Israel has fled before the Philistines and there has also been a great slaughter among the people. Also your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been taken."
AMP.18: When he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell off the seat backwards by the side of the [city] gate. His neck was broken and he died, for he was old and heavy. He had judged Israel for forty years.
AMP.19: Now his daughter-in-law, Phinehas' wife, was pregnant, and was about to give birth; so when she heard the news that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, she kneeled down and gave birth, because her [labor] pains began.
AMP.20: And about the time of her death [following the sudden birth] the women attending her said to her, "Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son." But she did not answer or pay any attention.
AMP.21: And she named the boy Ichabod, saying, "The glory has left Israel," because the ark of God had been taken and because of [the deaths of] her father-in-law and her husband.
AMP.22: She said, "The glory has left Israel, for the ark of God has been taken."

WEB.1: The word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, and encamped beside Ebenezer; and the Philistines encamped in Aphek.
WEB.2: The Philistines put themselves in array against Israel. When they joined battle, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men of the army in the field.
WEB.3: When the people had come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why has Yahweh defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us get the ark of Yahweh’s covenant out of Shiloh and bring it to us, that it may come among us, and save us out of the hand of our enemies.”
WEB.4: So the people sent to Shiloh; and they brought from there the ark of the covenant of Yahweh of Armies, who sits above the cherubim: and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
WEB.5: When the ark of Yahweh’s covenant came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth rang again.
WEB.6: When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, “What does the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” They understood that Yahweh’s ark had come into the camp.
WEB.7: The Philistines were afraid, for they said, “God has come into the camp.” They said, “Woe to us! For there has not been such a thing before.
WEB.8: Woe to us! Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods that struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
WEB.9: Be strong, and behave like men, O you Philistines, that you not be servants to the Hebrews, as they have been to you. Strengthen yourselves like men, and fight!”
WEB.10: The Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. There was a very great slaughter; for thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell.
WEB.11: God’s ark was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.
WEB.12: A man of Benjamin ran out of the army, and came to Shiloh the same day, with his clothes torn, and with dirt on his head.
WEB.13: When he came, behold, Eli was sitting on his seat by the road watching; for his heart trembled for God’s ark. When the man came into the city and told about it, all the city cried out.
WEB.14: When Eli heard the noise of the crying, he said, “What does the noise of this tumult mean?” The man hurried, and came and told Eli.
WEB.15: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old. His eyes were set, so that he could not see.
WEB.16: The man said to Eli, “I am he who came out of the army, and I fled today out of the army.” He said, “How did the matter go, my son?”
WEB.17: He who brought the news answered, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been also a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and God’s ark has been captured.”
WEB.18: When he made mention of God’s ark, Eli fell from off his seat backward by the side of the gate; and his neck broke, and he died; for he was an old man, and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.
WEB.19: His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to be delivered. When she heard the news that God’s ark was taken, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth; for her pains came on her.
WEB.20: About the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, “Don’t be afraid; for you have given birth to a son.” But she didn’t answer, neither did she regard it.
WEB.21: She named the child Ichabod,  saying, “The glory has departed from Israel”; because God’s ark was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
WEB.22: She said, “The glory has departed from Israel; for God’s ark has been taken.”

CSB17.1: And Samuel’s words came to all Israel. Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle and <sup>[1]</sup> camped at Ebenezer <sup>ⓑ</sup> while the Philistines camped at Aphek. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.2: The Philistines lined up in battle formation against Israel, and as the battle intensified, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men on the battlefield.
CSB17.3: When the troops returned to the camp, the elders of Israel asked, “Why did the LORD defeat us today before the Philistines? <sup>ⓓ</sup> Let’s bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant from Shiloh. Then it <sup>[2]</sup> will go with us and save us from our enemies.” <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.4: So the people sent men to Shiloh to bring back the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Armies, who is enthroned between the cherubim. <sup>ⓕ</sup> Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
CSB17.5: When the ark of the covenant of the LORD entered the camp, all the Israelites raised such a loud shout that the ground shook. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.6: The Philistines heard the sound of the war cry and asked, “What’s this loud shout in the Hebrews’ camp?” When the Philistines discovered that the ark of the LORD had entered the camp,
CSB17.7: they panicked. “A god has entered their camp!” they said. “Woe to us, nothing like this has happened before. <sup>[3]</sup>
CSB17.8: Woe to us, who will rescue us from these magnificent gods? These are the gods that slaughtered the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
CSB17.9: Show some courage and be men, Philistines! <sup>ⓗ</sup> Otherwise, you’ll serve the Hebrews just as they served you. <sup>ⓘ</sup> Now be men and fight!”
CSB17.10: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, <sup>ⓙ</sup> and each man fled to his tent. <sup>ⓚ</sup> The slaughter was severe — thirty thousand of the Israelite foot soldiers fell.
CSB17.11: The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.12: That same day, a Benjaminite man ran <sup>ⓜ</sup> from the battle and came to Shiloh. His clothes were torn, <sup>ⓝ</sup> and there was dirt on his head.
CSB17.13: When he arrived, there was Eli sitting on his chair beside the road watching, <sup>ⓐ</sup> because he was anxious about the ark of God. When the man entered the city to give a report, the entire city cried out.
CSB17.14: Eli heard the outcry and asked, “Why this commotion?” The man quickly came and reported to Eli.
CSB17.15: At that time Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes didn’t move <sup>[4]</sup> because he couldn’t see. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.16: The man said to Eli, “I’m the one who came from the battle. <sup>[5]</sup> I fled from there today.” “What happened, my son?” <sup>ⓒ</sup> Eli asked.
CSB17.17: The messenger answered, “Israel has fled from the Philistines, and also there was a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are both dead, and the ark of God has been captured.”
CSB17.18: When he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backward off the chair by the city gate, <sup>ⓓ</sup> and since he was old and heavy, his neck broke and he died. Eli had judged Israel forty years.
CSB17.19: Eli’s daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. When she heard the news about the capture of God’s ark and the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband, she collapsed and gave birth because her labor pains came on her.
CSB17.20: As she was dying, <sup>[6]</sup> the women taking care of her said, “Don’t be afraid. You’ve given birth to a son!” <sup>ⓔ</sup> But she did not respond or pay attention.
CSB17.21: She named the boy Ichabod, <sup>[7]</sup> saying, “The glory has departed from Israel,” <sup>ⓕ</sup> referring to the capture of the ark of God <sup>ⓖ</sup> and to the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband.
CSB17.22: “The glory has departed from Israel,” she said, “because the ark of God has been captured.”

MSG.1: Whatever Samuel said was broadcast all through Israel. Israel went to war against the Philistines. Israel set up camp at Ebenezer, the Philistines at Aphek.
MSG.2: The Philistines marched out to meet Israel, the fighting spread, and Israel was badly beaten—about 4,000 soldiers left dead on the field.
MSG.3: When the troops returned to camp, Israel's elders said, "Why has God given us such a beating today by the Philistines? Let's go to Shiloh and get the Chest of God's Covenant. It will accompany us and save us from the grip of our enemies."
MSG.4: So the army sent orders to Shiloh. They brought the Chest of the Covenant of God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, the Cherubim-Enthroned-God. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, accompanied the Chest of the Covenant of God.
MSG.5: When the Chest of the Covenant of God was brought into camp, everyone gave a huge cheer. The shouts were like thunderclaps shaking the very ground.
MSG.6:
The Philistines heard the shouting and wondered what on earth was going on: "What's all this shouting among the Hebrews?"
Then they learned that the Chest of God had entered the Hebrew camp.
MSG.7: The Philistines panicked: "Their gods have come to their camp! Nothing like this has ever happened before.
MSG.8: We're done for! Who can save us from the clutches of these supergods? These are the same gods who hit the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues out in the wilderness.
MSG.9: On your feet, Philistines! Courage! We're about to become slaves to the Hebrews, just as they have been slaves to us. Show what you're made of! Fight for your lives!"
MSG.10: And did they ever fight! It turned into a rout. They thrashed Israel so mercilessly that the Israelite soldiers ran for their lives, leaving behind an incredible 30,000 dead.
MSG.11: As if that wasn't bad enough, the Chest of God was taken and the two sons of Eli—Hophni and Phinehas—were killed.
MSG.12: Immediately, a Benjaminite raced from the front lines back to Shiloh. Shirt torn and face smeared with dirt,
MSG.13: he entered the town. Eli was sitting on his stool beside the road keeping vigil, for he was extremely worried about the Chest of God. When the man ran straight into town to tell the bad news, everyone wept.
MSG.14: They were appalled. Eli heard the loud wailing and asked, "Why this uproar?" The messenger hurried over and reported.
MSG.15: Eli was ninety-eight years old then, and blind.
MSG.16:
The man said to Eli, "I've just come from the front, barely escaping with my life."
"And so, my son," said Eli, "what happened?"
MSG.17: The messenger answered, "Israel scattered before the Philistines. The defeat was catastrophic, with enormous losses. Your sons Hophni and Phinehas died, and the Chest of God was taken."
MSG.18: At the words, "Chest of God," Eli fell backwards off his stool where he sat next to the gate. Eli was an old man, and very fat. When he fell, he broke his neck and died. He had led Israel forty years.
MSG.19: His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and ready to deliver. When she heard that the Chest of God had been taken and that both her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she went to her knees to give birth, going into hard labor.
MSG.20: As she was about to die, her midwife said, "Don't be afraid. You've given birth to a son!" But she gave no sign that she had heard.
MSG.21: The Chest of God gone, father-in-law dead, husband dead, she named the boy Ichabod (Glory's-Gone),
MSG.22: saying, "Glory is exiled from Israel since the Chest of God was taken."

NET.1: Samuel revealed the word of the LORD to all Israel. Then the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They camped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
NET.2: The Philistines arranged their forces to fight Israel. As the battle spread out, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men in the battle line in the field.
NET.3: When the army came back to the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why did the LORD let us be defeated today by the Philistines? Let’s take with us the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh. When it is with us, it will save us from the hand of our enemies.
NET.4: So the army sent to Shiloh, and they took from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts who sits between the cherubim. Now the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phineas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
